page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Slimy Limey!
title: Slimy Limey!
description:
How do you say no politely? Anna needs help following the call from Mr Lime asking her out to lunch. She wants to say no, but doesn’t want to sound rude. Her dilemma is how to refuse his offer politely. She finally plucks up the courage to call him, but how does he respond?
This episode focuses on politely refusing a request to do something.
phrases: Thank you for your offer. But I'm really sorry, I won't be able to.
I'm afraid it is against company policy…
With regret, I'm going to have to say no.

listening_challenge.question: What excuse does Anna give Seb Lime for not going to lunch with him?
listening_challenge.answer: She says it is against company policy.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello! You're joining us again after Anna's call from Mr Lime – he asked her to lunch, remember. Now Anna and Denise are flapping.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: ...and before you know it, he'll be asking you to marry him! Trust me Anna, this has happened to me dozens of times!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But I thought he was only interested in the lemons! Please promise me you won’t mention this to anyone.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Mr Lime has asked Anna to lunch!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: And it's not to talk business! I saw him looking at her with big eyes, from the moment he first saw her!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Old Slimy Limey eh? Lucky Anna!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Don't tell me you said yes?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well I didn't know what to say.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, no, I said I was busy and would call back. I wanted to just say no, but with everyone complaining that I'm not polite on the phone... I just... I didn't know how to say it politely.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ha ha, I'll tell you what to say.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hang on, let me write it down... why do all the pens keep disappearing?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Go away Slimy Limey. Are you sure?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
Don't listen to him Anna. This is what you should say:
Thank you for your offer. But I'm really sorry, I won't be able to.
Then explain why, say I'm afraid… blah blah blah

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Say it's against company policy to have non-business lunches with clients.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text:
You're not allowed to if it's not for business. Then say:
It wouldn't be appropriate. So, with regret, I'm going to have to say no.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text:
Okay, I think I've got that all down. Thanks. He'll be waiting for my call.
(dials phone)

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: Anna! Please, call me Seb. So, when can I invite you to lunch?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (whispering loudly) Thank you for your offer...

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, thank you for your offer. But I'm really sorry, I won't be able to.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm afraid it's against company policy to have non-business lunches with people.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, not shhh you Mr Slimy I meant shhhh Denise!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no! I mean Mr Limey – Lime – er Seb! You see, it wouldn't be appropriate. So, with regret, I'm going to have to say no.

transcript.speaker: Mr Lime
transcript.text: I think I've understood. Goodbye Anna.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear, he didn't take that too well. But, apart from a little mistake, Anna did well there. Here are the phrases she used to politely refuse the offer of lunch:
Good job Anna, bad luck Mr Slimy!
